title: GST reverse charge and Overseas Vendor Registration from 1 January 2020
summary: From 1 January 2020, GST-registered persons not entitled to full input tax credit must account for GST under reverse charge on B2B imported services, and overseas vendors must register and collect the prevailing standard GST rate on B2C digital services (Overseas Vendor Registration). Both paths use the then-prevailing 7% standard rate. From 1 January 2023 the same regimes were extended to low-value goods (and OVR also to B2C remote non-digital services); that later extension is recorded in the 8% rate versions and is not a separate pack diff.

changes.summary: Reverse charge on B2B imported services begins, at the prevailing standard rate of 7%, for GST-registered recipients who are not entitled to full input tax credit.

migration_impact.summary: Partial-exempt and other non-full-credit GST-registered persons must identify imported services, account for output tax at 7%, and report the value in GST F5 (Boxes 1, 5 and 14).

after.description: Reverse charge at the prevailing standard rate, from 1 January 2020.

changes.summary: Overseas Vendor Registration begins for B2C digital services. Qualifying overseas vendors collect the prevailing standard GST rate of 7%; this is not reverse charge.

migration_impact.summary: Overseas vendors of B2C digital services to Singapore customers must assess the S$1m / S$100,000 thresholds, register if liable, and charge 7% GST.

computation.notes: Standard rate collected by the overseas vendor.

after.description: OVR collection of the standard rate on B2C digital services.
